text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The prosecutor general's office passed to court the case of former prime minister Adolfas Slezevicius suspected of abuse of his position while getting higher interest rates for his private deposits than other clients of the bank. The trial is expected to start at the beginning of next year.
- Ceslovas Jursenas will continue to head the Lithuanian Democratic Labour party.
- The draft budget project of 1997 has been drawn up without understanding the Lithuanian economy, experts claim. The draft budget project plans 697 million litas deficit in 1997.
- All banks collected the required 20 million litas minimum share capital.

- The information in foreign press that ancient Jewish books and periodicals are stored in an inadequate manner do not respond to reality, said the chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbergis after his visit to National library on Saturday.
